CVD Predictors

Cardiovascular Disease Risk Prediction and Analysis

Author

Nicholas Tison

Published

September 25, 2026

Data Analysis Project

Predicting cardiovascular disease risk using clinical and demographic indicators.

This project evaluates how health factors such as age, blood pressure, cholesterol, and lifestyle behaviors relate to cardiovascular disease risk. The analysis is designed to support informed, evidence-based interpretation of patient risk and public health trends.

Objective

The goal of this analysis is to identify the strongest predictors of cardiovascular disease and to summarize the relationship between key health indicators and disease outcomes. By examining both risk factors and demographic trends, this project provides a clear, professional overview of cardiovascular risk assessment.

Risk Factors and Modifiable Behaviors

The World Heart Observatory identifies several major contributors to cardiovascular risk. These factors are especially important because many are modifiable through prevention, public health policy, and lifestyle change.

Risk factor Why it matters Prevention focus
Smoking Increases vascular damage, blood pressure, and clotting risk. Tobacco cessation and public health policy
Diet quality High sodium and poor diet patterns contribute to hypertension and systemic inflammation. Reduced sodium intake and healthier eating patterns
Air pollution Exposure is linked with blood vessel injury and elevated cardiovascular burden. Cleaner air policies and reduced pollution exposure
Hypertension It is a leading modifiable driver of heart attack, stroke, and cardiac strain. Blood-pressure screening and treatment
Obesity and inactivity These behaviors worsen metabolic health and increase long-term CVD risk. Activity promotion, nutrition, and weight management

Research Questions

  1. Which variables are most strongly associated with cardiovascular disease risk?
  2. How do behavioral and clinical characteristics influence disease likelihood?
  3. What insights can be drawn for risk stratification and public health planning?

Methodology

This analysis uses a structured approach that combines descriptive statistics, comparative analysis, and interpretation of risk predictors. Key variables are examined for patterns and relationships, with attention to how they contribute to cardiovascular disease risk in a real-world health context.

Key Findings

The preliminary findings suggest that cardiovascular risk is shaped by a combination of demographic, clinical, and behavioral factors. Age, blood pressure, cholesterol, and lifestyle indicators stand out as important contributors to overall risk. These findings underscore the importance of multifactor risk assessment rather than relying on any single measure.

Conclusion

This project demonstrates how data analysis can be used to investigate health outcomes in a systematic and interpretable way. By presenting the results in a clear, evidence-based format, the analysis supports data-driven discussion of cardiovascular risk and prevention strategies.
